title: ECG (Electrocardiogram)
description: Patient information about resting ECG testing at Woolloongabba Medical Centre, including preparation, results, follow-up and costs.
headings: Know about fees before you attend.
Patient guides for this area of care.
text: Medical Procedures ECG (Electrocardiogram) An electrocardiogram (ECG) is a simple, painless test that records the electrical activity of the heart. Procedure information What this care involves. An ECG can provide useful information about heart rhythm and electrical activity. It may be used when assessing symptoms such as palpitations or chest discomfort, monitoring some medicines, or investigating other heart-related concerns. An ECG is only one part of clinical assessment. What happens during the appointment? Small adhesive electrodes are placed on the chest and limbs and connected to the ECG machine. You lie still while the tracing is recorded. The test itself is brief and does not send electricity into your body. This page provides general information only. The treating clinician will explain what is appropriate for your individual circumstances and obtain consent where a procedure is planned. Before your appointment How to book and prepare. How to book Book a GP appointment or call reception if an ECG has already been requested. The team can confirm whether the ECG is performed as part of the consultation or requires a specific appointment sequence. Book Appointment Call (07) 3217 3344 Before your appointment No special preparation is usually required for a resting ECG. Wear clothing that allows access to the chest and limbs. Skin may need to be cleaned or small areas shaved so electrodes can attach properly. After your appointment Follow-up and aftercare. There is usually no recovery time after a resting ECG. A clinician will interpret the tracing together with your symptoms and history. Depending on the findings, you may need no further action, repeat assessment, blood tests, monitoring, imaging or specialist review. Costs Know about fees before you attend. Exact additional fees are confirmed before treatment. The standard Medicare-eligible GP consultation is bulk billed in line with the practice billing policy. An ECG or associated testing may involve an additional test/procedure charge depending on the clinical context. Reception will confirm the current practice charge before the appointment wherever practical. External investigations or specialist appointments are billed separately by those providers. Read Fees & Billing Patient questions Frequently Asked Questions Does an ECG hurt? A resting ECG is painless. Adhesive electrodes are placed on the skin to record the heart’s electrical activity. How long does an ECG take? The recording itself is brief, but allow time for preparation, the clinical assessment and discussion of results. Can a normal ECG rule out every heart problem? No. An ECG records the heart during the test and must be interpreted with symptoms and other information. Further testing may still be needed. What if I have severe chest pain now? Do not wait for a routine ECG appointment. Call Triple Zero (000) for severe or life-threatening symptoms. More information Trusted information and related care. title: Radiology
description: Information about independent on-site radiology and diagnostic imaging, including referrals, preparation, reports and provider fees.
headings: How to access the service and prepare.
Know who is responsible for fees.
Patient guides for this area of care.
text: Independent On-Site Service Radiology Patients can access radiology and diagnostic imaging through an independent third-party provider on site. The radiology service is not owned or operated by Woolloongabba Medical Centre. Service information Accessing radiology services. Diagnostic imaging can include different types of scans and imaging tests used to investigate symptoms, injuries or medical conditions. The modalities available on site, appointment requirements and reporting arrangements are determined by the independent radiology provider. Your GP or specialist can discuss whether imaging is appropriate and provide a referral when required. Independent provider. This service is provided by a separate third-party business and is not owned or operated by Woolloongabba Medical Centre. Provider availability, opening hours, service scope, fees and billing can change independently of the medical centre. Before you attend How to access the service and prepare. How to access radiology Bring the imaging referral supplied by your clinician. Contact the radiology provider to confirm whether the requested imaging is available on site and whether you need an appointment. Before imaging Preparation depends on the test. Some imaging may require fasting, drinking water, a full bladder, removal of metal items or specific instructions about medicines or contrast. Follow the instructions provided by the radiology service and tell them about pregnancy, allergies, kidney problems or implanted devices where relevant. After the service Results, medicines and follow-up. The radiology provider prepares the report and normally sends it to the clinician who requested the imaging. Arrange follow-up with the referring clinician as advised so the report can be interpreted together with your symptoms, examination and other tests. Costs Know who is responsible for fees. Third-party provider fees are separate. Radiology fees are set and billed by the independent imaging provider. Medicare may cover some or all of the cost of eligible diagnostic imaging, depending on the test, referral and Medicare rules. Ask the radiology provider about its current fee and any out-of-pocket amount before the test. A GP consultation at Woolloongabba Medical Centre is billed separately under the medical centre billing policy. Read Woolloongabba Medical Centre Fees & Billing Patient questions Frequently Asked Questions Do I need a referral? Many diagnostic imaging services require a referral from a GP or specialist. Bring the referral and confirm the provider requirements when making the imaging booking. Is every type of scan available on site? Not necessarily. Available imaging types, equipment and appointment times are controlled by the independent radiology provider. Confirm availability directly with the provider. Who explains the imaging report? The clinician who requested the imaging is usually best placed to explain the report and what it means for your care. Book follow-up as advised. Is radiology operated by the medical centre? No. The on-site radiology service is an independent third-party provider. Its clinical services, staffing, bookings, fees and billing are separate from Woolloongabba Medical Centre.
